english.title: Commit fraud / be the party to the fraudulent use of weighing / measuring equipment for trade use
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..)

(A)_[committed]_
(B)_[were party to the commission of]_

fraud in the using of

(C)_[weighing]_
(D)_[measuring]_

english.legislation: Contrary to sections 17(3) and 84(4)(a) of the Weights and Measures Act 1985.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
committed / were party to the commission of fraud
in the using of weighing / measuring equipment for trade

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Section 17(1) of the Weights and Measures Act 1985 provides that the equipment shall be liable to be forfeited.
(ii) Section 83(1) of the Weights and Measures Act 1985 provides that in England and Wales, proceedings for any offence under this Act or any instrument made under this Act. shall not be instituted except by or on behalf of a local weights and measures authority or the chief officer of police for a police area.

other.penalty:
Summary: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
